intro: Vanuatu is a Y-shaped chain of about 80 islands that was once ruled jointly by Britain and France.

chapters.title: Lapita and chiefs
text: Lapita people arrived about 3,000 years ago. Roi Mata, a great chief of the 1600s, is honoured at a World Heritage site.

chapters.title: The Condominium
text: From 1906 Britain and France ruled together in an unusual 'Condominium', with two police forces, two school systems and two sets of laws. In the 1800s many ni-Vanuatu were taken, sometimes by force, to work on plantations in Australia and Fiji, a practice called blackbirding.

highlight.title: Two rulers
highlight.text: The New Hebrides was jointly ruled by Britain and France.

chapters.title: Independence
text: Vanuatu became independent in 1980. Cyclone Pam in 2015 and a strong earthquake in 2024 caused great damage. Vanuatu led a successful push for a UN court opinion on climate change, delivered in 2025.

timeline.title: Climate ruling
timeline.text: A UN court opinion Vanuatu sought.

keyTerms.meaning: A territory ruled by two countries together.
